role.altitude: The hydro production manager keeps inspecting turbines and switchyards, supervising operations, planning outages and dealing with the trader and water authority; paper inspection lists, writing work requests, tracking certificate dates and mailing forecasts shrink.
skills_to_grow: Setting limits on condition pages and keeping turbine curves current
role.ambitious_version: A manager whose forecasts and inspection records update themselves, so site visits go to what the data cannot show.

tasks.short: Review turbine and generator readings, monitor or inspect hydroelectric equipment on site, record findings, raise work requests and discuss them with maintenance.

steps.what: Hydro production manager monitors turbine, generator and control system readings: vibration, bearing temperatures and output
Hydro production manager inspects hydro-turbines, generators and control cabinets on site
Hydro production manager writes findings on a paper inspection list
Hydro production manager writes work requests for maintenance from the findings
Hydro production manager discusses findings and priorities with the maintenance lead

tasks.design: Condition pages in the plant's control system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) show vibration, bearing temperatures and output per unit against fixed limits, with trends over weeks, so the manager sees what to look at before going on site. On site the manager uses an inspection app with a checklist per unit, photos and readings; a finding marked for repair becomes a work request in the maintenance system with the photo attached. Inspecting and agreeing priorities stay with the manager. No learning model is used on the control system.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings were scanned screen by screen and findings written on paper and retyped as requests.
tasks.enabler_now: Condition pages on plant control systems, and inspection apps linked to maintenance systems.
tasks.still_hard: Faults that only show as sound, smell or heat on site.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing cavitation in a turbine before the sensors show it.
tasks.altitude: Less paperwork around inspections; inspecting stays on site.

reach.learn: Whether requests with photos need fewer questions back.

evidence.claim: Plant control systems show condition values against limits and trends; inspection apps create maintenance requests.
AI used as a safety component in electricity supply is an AI Act high-risk use; the design uses fixed limits only.

assumptions: Boundary: monitoring and inspecting equipment up to agreed priorities; repairs are maintenance work.
Input contract for s1: unit readings from the control system's sensors; limits set by the manager with the asset engineer.
Input contract for s4: findings the manager records in the app in s3; the app's link to the maintenance system, set up by the maintenance lead, creates the request.
On-site inspection and talks keep their full time.
unknowns: Whether the maintenance system accepts requests from an app.

already_counted.description: Hydro production manager checks app requests before they go to maintenance.

incremental.description: Hydro production manager keeps checklists and limits current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small plant with one unit and few findings; high: several units with frequent inspections and many findings.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan the round, inspect hydroelectric facilities including switchyards, control houses and relay houses for normal operation and safety standards, record readings and findings, follow them up and report to the asset owner.

steps.what: Hydro production manager plans the inspection round
Hydro production manager inspects switchyards, control houses and relay houses for normal operation and adherence to safety standards
Hydro production manager records readings and findings, such as battery voltages and relay counters, on paper
Hydro production manager follows up findings with maintenance and safety fixes
Hydro production manager reports inspection results to the asset owner

tasks.design: The inspection app holds the round schedule and a checklist per switchyard, control house and relay house; the manager enters the actual readings and findings on site with photos. Findings open follow-up items with owners and due dates, and the periodic report to the asset owner is generated from the round records. Walking the installations and judging their state stay with the manager.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rounds were recorded on paper and reports typed from the sheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Inspection apps with checklists, follow-up items and generated reports.
tasks.still_hard: Spotting a hazard that is not on any checklist.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing that a fence or sign has been tampered with.
tasks.altitude: Less writing after rounds; the inspection itself does not change.

reach.learn: Whether generated reports show trends across rounds.

evidence.claim: Inspection apps record checklists, readings and photos and generate reports.
No AI Act high-risk use arises from recording inspection results.

assumptions: Boundary: one inspection round to its report; repairs are outside.
Input contract for s3 and s5: actual readings and findings entered by the manager in the app on site; the report is built from those records only.
Coverage: the app works offline in the switchyard; where it cannot be used, the paper list is typed afterwards.
The inspection walk keeps its full time.
research_questions: Are findings closed faster when they have owners and due dates?

incremental.description: Hydro production manager keeps checklists current after installation changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: short rounds with few readings; high: large switchyards with many readings and monthly reports.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Supervise or monitor hydroelectric facility operations against water level and flow rules, check that generation and mechanical equipment conform to applicable regulations through inspection due dates, supervise staff and contractors, log deviations and report them, and check environmental conditions.

steps.what: Hydro production manager monitors operations against the water level and flow rules agreed with the water authority
Hydro production manager checks that equipment inspections and certificates for regulated generation and mechanical equipment are current
Hydro production manager supervises operators and contractors on site
Hydro production manager logs deviations and reports them to the water authority or grid operator when required
Hydro production manager checks environmental permit conditions such as fish protection measures

tasks.design: The control system shows water levels and flows against the bands agreed with the water authority, with alarms near the edges. A compliance register lists each regulated item of equipment with its last inspection, certificate and due date and reminds the manager in time. Deviations are logged in the plant's operations system ({OPS_SYSTEM}); reports to the water authority or grid operator stay with the manager. Supervision and environmental checks stay on site.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inspection due dates were kept in a spreadsheet that was checked by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Compliance registers with reminders and control system level bands.
tasks.still_hard: High water situations where rules and production pull apart.
tasks.human_edge: Working out with the water authority what to do at the edge of a band.
tasks.altitude: Fewer missed due dates; supervision stays in person.

reach.learn: Whether the register shows inspections at risk early enough.

evidence.claim: Records apps with due-date reminders replace compliance spreadsheets.
AI used as a safety component in electricity supply is an AI Act high-risk use; the design adds none.

assumptions: Boundary: supervising operations for conformance; carrying out inspections is done by inspectors and maintenance.
Input contract for s2: the compliance register built once from the inspection certificates by the asset engineer and updated when new certificates arrive.
Supervision, reporting and environmental checks keep their full or nearly full time.
unknowns: Number of regulated items of equipment.
research_questions: Are inspections ever overdue after the register goes live?

incremental.description: Asset engineer builds and keeps the compliance register.
Hydro production manager checks register reminders monthly.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few regulated items; high: many pressure, lifting and high-voltage items with different inspection cycles.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review river flow forecasts and level constraints, plan or coordinate hydroelectric production to meet customer requirements, plan outages with the trader and grid operator, confirm the forecast and have it sent to the trader, and handle deviations during the day.

steps.what: Hydro production manager reviews river flow forecasts and water level constraints
Hydro production manager plans the production forecast per hour to meet the customer requirements
Hydro production manager coordinates maintenance outages with the trader and grid operator
Hydro production manager confirms the final production forecast
Hydro production manager mails the production forecast to the energy trader
Hydro production manager handles deviations from the forecast with the trader during the day

approvals.approved_version: the production forecast as confirmed by the manager in s4; later changes are sent as a new version after a new confirmation

tasks.design: Published river flow forecasts are fetched into the planning sheet each morning, and fixed calculations turn the expected flow, head and the turbines' efficiency curves into an hourly production forecast, with outages taken out. The manager adjusts and confirms it, and the confirmed version goes to the trader's system by automatic file transfer instead of mail. Agreeing outages and handling deviations during the day stay with the manager. No learning model is used; the forecast is plain calculation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Flows were looked up and the forecast built by hand each day.
tasks.enabler_now: Published flow forecasts and file transfer to traders' systems.
tasks.still_hard: Sudden rain or upstream releases that the forecast misses.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing how the river behaves after a dry spell.
tasks.altitude: Less daily calculation; coordination stays with the manager.

reach.learn: Whether automatic forecasts arrive earlier and with fewer errors.

evidence.claim: Production forecasts for run-of-river plants follow from expected flow, head and turbine efficiency curves.
AI used as a safety component in electricity supply is an AI Act high-risk use; the forecast uses plain calculation.

assumptions: Boundary: daily production planning and coordination; trading is the trader's work.
Input contract for s1: river flow forecasts published by the water authority and fetched automatically; level constraints from the agreement with the water authority.
Input contract for s2: expected flows from s1, unit availability from the maintenance plan, and turbine efficiency curves kept by the asset engineer.
Input contract for s5: file transfer to the trader's system agreed with the trader.
Outage talks and deviations keep their full time.
unknowns: Whether the trader accepts automatic files.

already_counted.description: Hydro production manager adjusts the calculated forecast for known local effects.

incremental.description: Hydro production manager checks forecast against actual output weekly.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: stable river flows and few outages; high: changing flows with daily forecasts and frequent updates.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
